## Welcome

- Introductions
  * Name and Organization
  * Experience with TMB, R, C++
  * What are you hoping to learn
  * Special interest

## Why RTMB

- R wrapper for TMB
- Run R code in C++ for speed
- Automatic Differentiation
- Fit models with random effects (e.g. Laplace)
- Easy code checking in R

## Course Structure

- Can't code if you don't understand model
- Focus on understanding a model, then coding it in R
- RTMB is very simple if you know how to code a likelihood in R
- Will focus on understanding in the mornings and practical coding in the afternoon

## Learning Outcomes

- Understand how to fit a custom likelihood and report on it
- Basic programming in RTMB
- Fitting hierarchical models
- RTMB specific applications

## Outline Day 1

1. (9:00 – 10:00) Introduction to writing a likelihood with RTMB.
2. (10:00 - 11:00) Computing gradients and optimization
3. (11:00 – 12:00) Variance estimation and reporting
4. (12:00 - 13:00) Lunch
4. (13:00 – 14:00) Hierarchical models in RTMB
5. (14:00 – 15:00) Practice fitting hierarchical models.
6. (15:00 – 16:00) Additional random effect structures (e.g. time varying productivity). 

## Outline Day 2

1. (9:00 – 9:50) Variance estimation for maximum likelihood. Delta method to approximate parameters. Using RTMB to report variance and confidence intervals. 
2. (10:00 – 10:50) RTMB functionality. Learn little details about how to use RTMB effectively. 
3. (11:00 – 11:50) Writing helper functions and atomics (e.g. Lambert W). Best coding practices. 
4. (13:00 – 16:00) Practice writing complex likelihood functions in RTMB
